content: David Nicholson CBE is a senior administrator within the English National Health Service (NHS) and was appointed as its Chief Executive in September 2006. He earned a degree in History and Politics from Bristol University, graduating with a 2:1. During the 1970s, Nicholson was a member of the Communist Party, a membership he maintained until 1983. In 1988, he became the Chief Executive of the Doncaster Royal Infirmary NHS Trust during its first wave of establishment. While in this role, he implemented Clinical Directorates and led the Trust as a national pilot site for Total Quality Management. In 1997, he transitioned to the Trent NHS Regional Office, where he served as the Regional Director of Performance. By November 2000, he was promoted to the position of Regional Director. Between December 2001 and March 2002, Nicholson held the role of Regional Director for both the Eastern and West Midlands Regions, while simultaneously maintaining his responsibilities in the Trent region. During this period, he also served in a shadow capacity as the Director of Health and Social Care (designate) for the Midlands and East of England. In April 2002, he formally assumed the role of Director of Health and Social Care for the Midlands and East of England, overseeing eight Strategic Health Authorities and a population of 20 million. In 2003, Nicholson was appointed Chief Executive of the Birmingham and The Black Country Strategic Health Authority (BBC SHA). By August 2005, he had taken on additional responsibilities as Chief Executive of the neighboring Shropshire and Staffordshire SHA, as well as the West Midlands South SHA. In April 2006, he was named Chief Executive of the newly established London Strategic Health Authority. However, his tenure in this role was brief, as it was announced on July 27, 2006, that he would assume the position of NHS Chief Executive in September 2006. In this capacity, he was tasked with managing a £90 billion budget and overseeing 1.3 million employees. This marked his fifth job transition within a single year. Nicholson was recognized with a Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE) in the 2004 New Year Honours list. Additionally, he received an honorary Doctor of the University award from the University of Central England in Birmingham. He is the father of two sons—one a recent graduate and the other currently pursuing university studies. Nicholson is also an avid supporter of Nottingham Forest Football Club.
